title: Compose Multiplatform
learning_outcomes: Explain the central rule or purpose of compose multiplatform using at least one correct term from the lesson.
Interpret or adapt a small Kotlin example that demonstrates compose multiplatform.
Identify one relevant edge case, debugging step, or version/platform constraint.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will learn **Compose Multiplatform** as part of **Kotlin Multiplatform and Compose Multiplatform**. Android application code must respect lifecycle, UI-thread rules, accessibility, permission boundaries, and the compatibility of Android/Compose dependencies. Use the subtopics—Shared UI Fundamentals, Shared State and Navigation, Platform-Specific UI Considerations—as a checklist: predict what the example will do, then verify it in a project configured for the target platform.
content.why_it_matters: Multiplatform work succeeds when shared code depends only on common APIs and platform-specific code is isolated behind deliberate interfaces.

content_blocks.title: Common mistake to avoid
content_blocks.text: Compose Multiplatform removes the need to test boundary conditions or verify the chosen runtime/library version.

content_blocks.title: Troubleshooting and reset
content_blocks.text: If the example fails, first confirm which runtime/project type the snippet requires. Read the first useful compiler or runtime message, check imports and declared dependencies, reduce the example to a minimal case, and rerun. For target-specific code, use the target toolchain rather than assuming a console or browser runner can execute it.
